title: Photosynthesis — following matter and energy
summary: Trace carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen while light supplies energy.

sections.title: 1. Matter cycles; energy flows
sections.markdown: Plants use light energy to rearrange carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen. The balanced overview is $6CO_2 + 6H_2O → C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2$. Light provides energy but is not an atom in the products.

visualization.title: Matter and energy through a leaf
visualization.aria_label: Carbon dioxide, water, and light enter a leaf; glucose and oxygen leave the photosynthesis process.
visualization.text_fallback: Inputs are carbon dioxide, water, and light energy. Outputs are glucose and oxygen.

sections.title: 2. Chloroplasts capture light
sections.markdown: Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts. Chlorophyll absorbs light energy, which helps build energy-rich glucose. Cells can later release some of that stored chemical energy through cellular respiration.

sections.title: 3. Check atoms on both sides
sections.markdown: The balanced equation contains 6 carbon, 12 hydrogen, and 18 oxygen atoms on each side. Counting atoms shows that matter is conserved even though the molecules change.
